name: adwhispr
description:
AdWhispr gives Claude competitor ad intelligence and campaign execution.

Research: ingest any brand's entire public ad library from Meta and TikTok. Find verified competitors actually running ads in your niche right now, search ads semantically by concept ("social proof", "founder story"), pull a brand's TikTok ads with the proven winners first, and get real Google Keyword Planner data for any topic.

Briefs: generate a full competitive brief on any brand longevity curve, top hooks, longest-running winners, format mix, and a positioning verdict, with a downloadable PDF.

Execution: connect your own Meta, Google, or TikTok ad account once via OAuth, then launch complete campaigns from chat, Google Search, Performance Max, TikTok video, and Meta single-image or carousel ads from your own creative library. Every campaign is created paused with a preview-and-confirm step, so nothing spends until you explicitly resume it. Read performance, adjust budgets, and pause or resume campaigns conversationally.

Free tier included, no API keys to manage. Try: "Who has the best ads in my niche?" or "Launch a Google Search campaign for my store at $20/day."

protocolMetadata.instructions:
AdWhispr is a competitor-ad research and campaign execution platform. Use this short guide to choose tools correctly.

Common workflows:

★ Find the best competitor ads in the user's space (the most common request)
   • When the user asks "who has the best ads in my space", "show me winning ads for my product/niche", "who are my competitors", or anything similar WITHOUT naming a specific competitor: call get_my_brand FIRST to learn their product/niche. If nothing is saved, ask for their product page URL. The moment they reveal their business in ANY form — a link, their website, or just a plain description ("I sell X", "I run a Y", "we make Z"), even in passing — call save_my_brand to persist it (it takes a URL or a description), then continue researching without re-asking.
   • Then call find_competitors (it uses the saved brand automatically) and present its VERIFIED advertisers — brands checked, seconds ago, to be running ads right now, ranked by active-ad count. Keep its three buckets separate: lead with the verified advertisers, mention the "checked, not currently advertising" ones honestly, and never present the "couldn't verify" names as advertisers. Do NOT brainstorm competitor names from your own knowledge — your guesses may not advertise at all, which is the exact failure this tool prevents. Only if find_competitors returns nothing may you name competitors yourself, and if you do, say those names are unverified.
   • For a verified brand already in AdWhispr, use its brand ID with get_brand_ads (sortBy:longevity) to surface the proven winners. For a verified brand not tracked yet, offer to add_brand it (pass the pageId find_competitors gave you) and set the expectation that its ads take a minute or two to load. TWO ID TYPES, never mix them: a brandId is a UUID and is what get_brand_ads/get_brand_stats/search_ads take; a pageId is numeric and works ONLY in add_brand. tool.name: launch_cloned_ad
tool.title: Launch Cloned Ad
tool.description: Take an image clone the user already made in the AdWhispr web app (it lives in their Creative Library) and launch it as a real, PAUSED ad in their connected Meta account — campaign + ad set + creative + ad, all paused (no spend until they resume). This closes the loop: research a competitor → clone their winning ad in the AdWhispr app → launch it from here. ONLY the cloned IMAGE comes from the clone — the destination link and ad copy are the USER'S OWN: you MUST write message (primary text, and optionally headline) fresh for the user's product, and the link is the user's own page (falls back to their saved website; the competitor's URL and copy are NEVER used — the tool refuses without your own copy). Two-step: call without confirmToken for a preview + token — the preview shows the exact destination link and copy; show them to the user — then again with the confirmToken to create it. The ad runs from one of the user's Facebook Pages: pass pageName (e.g. "adWhispr") to pick it by name, and if the user has exactly one page enabled it is used automatically — you do NOT need a numeric pageId. Only pass pageId if the user gives you an explicit numeric id. If the page can't be resolved, the tool replies with the enabled page names to choose from. Get the clonedAdId from list_my_creatives. Objective is one of: traffic (default), sales, awareness, engagement — sales optimizes for purchases via the account's Meta pixel (attached automatically; a clear error explains if the account has none); lead objectives need a lead form and are not offered here. Targeting (interests, ages, gender, geo, retargeting audiences) is supported — resolve ids/keys with search_ad_targeting first. If the user has not said what the ad should achieve, ASK them to pick traffic, sales, awareness, or engagement before launching instead of guessing.

tool.name: launch_meta_ad
tool.title: Launch Meta Ad (own images, video, or carousel)
tool.description: Launch the user's OWN images or videos as a real, PAUSED ad in their connected Meta (Facebook/Instagram) account — campaign + ad set + creative + ad, all paused (no spend until they resume). ONE image card = a single-image ad; 2–10 image cards = a CAROUSEL in the exact card order given; ONE video card = a VIDEO ad. MIXED cards (a video plus images, or several videos, 2–10 total) = a CREATIVE TEST: each card becomes its OWN ad inside ONE shared ad set, and Meta shifts the ad set's budget toward whichever ad performs — use this when the user wants several creatives competing (e.g. 'test my video against these two photos'). Use this when the user has their own finished creatives ('launch my carousel', 'run this image I made', 'launch my video on Facebook') — for launching an image clone made in the AdWhispr app use launch_cloned_ad instead; finished AI videos made in the app land in the Creative Library and launch HERE by creativeName. WHERE CREATIVES COME FROM: the user's Creative Library — reference each card by creativeName (see list_my_creatives; images and videos both work). If their files aren't uploaded yet, send them to https://adwhispr.com/dashboard/creatives to upload (drag & drop), then have them tell you when done and use list_my_creatives to find the names. A direct https imageUrl/videoUrl the user owns also works. NEVER use competitor images or ad-library assets. On confirm, a video is uploaded into the ad account and Meta processes it (~30s extra; if processing outruns the call, the campaign + ad set are still created and the tool says how to finish). Per-card headline/description/link are optional (link falls back to the ad-level link, which falls back to the user's saved website). The ad runs from one of the user's Facebook Pages: pass pageName to pick by name; with exactly one enabled page it's used automatically — a numeric pageId is not needed. Objective: traffic (default), sales (auto-attaches the account's Meta pixel), awareness, or engagement — if the user cares about the goal but hasn't said which, ASK; otherwise default to traffic. TARGETING: never interrogate the user about targeting — only set the params they explicitly asked for (resolve ids via search_ad_targeting); everything else uses defaults and the preview states exactly what was applied (marked '(default)') so the user can adjust before confirming. Two-step: call without confirmToken for a preview + token, then again with the confirmToken to create it. EDIT AN EXISTING AD: pass editAdId plus the new message/headline/link to change a live or paused ad's copy in place (no new campaign; before-vs-after preview, then confirm; the edited ad re-enters Meta review). RADIUS TARGETING: radiusAddress + radiusKm target a circle around a street address ('everyone within 10 km of my shop'). RETARGETING: set retargetWebsiteVisitors:true to CREATE a website-visitors audience from the account's Meta pixel and target this ad at it in one step ('retarget people who visited my site') — optional retargetRetentionDays (1-180, default 30) and retargetExcludePurchasers; the audience spends nothing by itself. To target an audience that ALREADY exists instead, pass its id via audienceIds (from search_ad_targeting kind 'audiences').

userOs.description: Mobile OS targeting, e.g. ["iOS"] to reach iPhone/iPad users only (implies mobile-only delivery). ONLY set this when the user explicitly asks for it (e.g. "target iOS users", "iPhone owners") — NEVER prompt the user about OS or device targeting.

ctaType.description: Call-to-action button, e.g. LEARN_MORE (default), SHOP_NOW, SIGN_UP, GET_OFFER, BOOK_NOW, CALL_NOW, WHATSAPP_MESSAGE. CALL_NOW makes a click-to-call ad and REQUIRES phoneNumber. WHATSAPP_MESSAGE makes a click-to-WhatsApp ad — pass the wa.me link as `link` and the ad set is pointed at the chat automatically. interests.description: Meta interest ids from search_ad_targeting (kind "interests"). Never invent ids — always search first and confirm the picks with the user.

objective.description: The campaign goal, defaults to traffic. Sales optimizes for purchases via the account's Meta pixel (attached automatically; a clear error explains if the account has none). Leads means WEBSITE leads via the pixel Lead event by default — UNLESS you pass leadFormId, which switches it to an on-Meta instant form (no pixel).

leadFormId.description: On-Meta lead ads: the id of an instant (lead) form the user ALREADY built in Meta Ads Manager. Only valid with objective "leads". The ad then captures leads INSIDE Facebook/Instagram via that form (no pixel, no website hop) — ideal when conversions happen off-site or there is no pixel. Prerequisites the user handles once: their Facebook Page must have accepted Facebook's Lead Generation Terms, and the ad needs an external destination link. A clear steer explains if either is missing.

regionKeys.description: Region/state keys from search_ad_targeting (kind "locations"). Never invent keys. When set, countries are ignored (Meta forbids overlapping locations).

radiusAddress.description: RADIUS targeting: a street address or place to target AROUND (e.g. "Hoofdstraat 12, Amsterdam"). Meta locates the address itself — no lookup needed. When set, all other geo params are ignored (one circle IS the geography). Use when the user wants "within X km of my shop/city/address".

devicePlatforms.description: Device platforms to target, e.g. ["mobile"]. ONLY set this when the user explicitly asks to target by device — NEVER ask the user about device targeting; the default (all devices) is correct for most launches, and the preview will state it.

retargetWebsiteVisitors.description: When true, CREATE a website-visitors audience from the account's Meta pixel and target this ad at it (retargeting). Needs a pixel on the account — a clear error explains if there is none. The audience spends nothing by itself.

retargetExcludePurchasers.description: Retargeting only: exclude people who purchased in the last 180 days
